extracted.intended_audience: NIH K01/other NIH grant applicants and institutional investigators preparing Facilities & Other Resources and biographical sketch sections
extracted.subtask_description: Assembling the Facilities & Other Resources, Data Management, Foreign Justification, and Biographical Sketch/Profile sections of an NIH K01 (career development) grant application, documenting institutional supports, IT/data infrastructure, and required investigator CV formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional centers and collaborations supporting the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of centers (e.g., Global WACh, PERLA, Global Medicines Program, Center for Health and the Global Environment, Health Alliance International) demonstrate institutional programs that 'make scientific discoveries, cultivate leaders, and bridge disciplines' and partner with ministries and field sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List institutional centers/units and explain how they provide interdisciplinary collaborations, field staff, local partnerships, or expertise relevant to the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library resources and access
rubrics_metrics.description: The University of Washington Libraries will support the proposed project by making the latest scientific articles and other resources on dissemination science, social marketing, health promotion, and workplaces available to the investigator team. The Health Sciences Libraries include >350,000 bound volumes and ~2,400 current journal subscriptions, desktop (including remote/off-campus) access to thousands of electronic journals at no cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document library holdings, remote electronic access for investigators, and linkages (e.g., NN/LM Pacific Northwest Regional services, librarian expertise) that facilitate literature access and information assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document delivery service levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Document delivery via e-mail for items not available in the electronic journal collection is available 24 hours a day with normal (within 24 hours of request) or rush (within 4 hours of request) turn-around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State expected turnaround times for obtaining articles/documents, distinguishing normal vs. rush service to demonstrate timely access to literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core institutional support services
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the support services at the University of Washington are available for the use of staff, trainees and faculty. These include a machine shop, electronics shop, computer graphics services, photographic services, and financial management services. There is daily courier service between UW, Fred Hutchinson, Harborview, and several clinics and research sites to transport specimens and materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate core technical/administrative services and specimen/material transport infrastructure that will support study operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General computing resources and negotiated software licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: University-supported resources include Ethernet access and various databases (Current Index to Statistics, Medline, UW library catalog, Library of Congress). The University negotiates group-discounted site licenses for widely used software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional network/database access, available licensed software, and how these support data analysis and literature searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebula Managed Desktop Services and UW Google Apps availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Nebula Managed Desktop Services includes delivery and installation of Nebula software suite, phone support, private and shared file server space, security (patching, anti-virus, hot fixes), drive mappings, printer installs, file restores, and basic set-up for Outlook. UW Google Apps provides web-based applications integrated with UW email (Email with >7 GB, Calendar, Talk, Docs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document desktop management, integrated collaboration tools, and helpdesk/phone support available to project staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning and Scholarly Technologies (LST) training and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: UW LST offers free workshops on software (Adobe Creative Suite, Photoshop), online curriculum in computing fundamentals, design/graphics, digital audio/video, document creation, spreadsheets and databases, and web publishing. LST offers a free online suite including an online survey tool, file sharing, and shared work space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note availability of institutional training and web-based tools that can build team capacity and support project tasks (surveys, file sharing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel computing hardware, software, and baseline security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of the ICRC team are supplied with laptops, desktops, printers, peripherals and software; four faculty use Apple laptops with Bootcamp/Fusion for Windows compatibility. All computers are required to have Sophos anti-virus software. Specialized software provided to personnel with demonstrated need includes SAS, SPSS, Stata, Epi Info, R, S Plus, Endnote, Adobe Acrobat Professional, Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator, Microsoft Project and Visio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the standard hardware/software provided to personnel and mandatory security software to demonstrate staff capacity and baseline cybersecurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure file servers and backup procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICRC utilizes secure file servers managed by UW IT services. The servers have remote and local access capabilities, and are backed up daily with redundant backup storage off site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document server hosting, backup frequency, off-site redundancy, and remote access capabilities to show data persistence and disaster recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access control and restricted data sections
rubrics_metrics.description: File folders on the server are restricted to ICRC-specific user groups, whose membership are regularly reviewed and maintained. Files are password-protected when deemed necessary. A restricted section of the server is reserved for the data team who have exclusive password-protected access. Changes to server access are carefully monitored and must be approved before implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe role-based access controls, periodic review of permissions, use of password protection, and formal approval processes for changes to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house IT support, redundancy, and travel readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary IT support is provided in house. Services include on-demand software support, hardware troubleshooting, general technical support, computing services research, smartphone and A/V support. Travelling employees have access to support and have redundant systems including remote backup, secure external hard drives and travel readiness sessions. Additional post-travel computer check-ups are performed. IT support is available 24 hours a day in conjunction with UW IT services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document availability of continuous IT support, procedures for travel readiness and post-travel checks, and redundancy measures for traveling staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central Specimen Repository IT and scanning infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICRC Central Specimen Repository has 3 computers and 2 barcode scanners for scanning incoming/outgoing specimens. The computers link to a dedicated in-house server hosting the Repository Freezerworks database which is backed up nightly. Service is provided both in house and by the UW Health Sciences server group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specimen tracking hardware (barcode scanners), dedicated database software, and nightly backups to demonstrate specimen data integrity and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documented existing equipment inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing equipment is enumerated in the Facilities and Other Resources pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an equipment list (copiers, printers, scanners, specialized instruments) and indicate availability to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of DF/Net Research, Inc. and DataFax closed system for data management
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICRC contracts with DF/Net Research, Inc. to perform data management tasks using DataFax, an off-the-shelf study and data management software package that uses fax machines, bar codes, and intelligent character recognition (ICR) to collect and monitor clinical study data. DataFax is considered a closed system; images of case report forms are processed by ICR software and stored in a proprietary database. All CRF images remain electronic within DataFax throughout the data management process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe vendor/data system, 'closed system' status, data flow (image capture → ICR → proprietary DB), and continuous electronic storage of CRFs to show data provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DataFax security and audit trails
rubrics_metrics.description: Security is included at the system, DataFax, and procedural level to limit data access to authorized individuals. All transactions are fully recorded in a secure audit trail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document multilayer security controls and complete transaction/audit logging to support data integrity and compliance with regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-limited in-house access via iDataFax and portal controls
rubrics_metrics.description: In house data staff are provided with view-only access to a study’s DataFax database via iDataFax, designed for users who need specific access to view subject CRFs, data, and data queries in a role that does not allow changing data. In-house staff are provided access to view and download study reports and/or CRFs via the DF/Net web portal. Changes to access of this portal must be approved before implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe role-limited interfaces (view-only vs. edit), portal access for report/CRF downloads, and formal approval workflows for access changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of REDCap for electronic data capture
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICRC has access to REDCap hosted at the Institute of Translational Health Sciences. REDCap is a free, secure, web-based application providing: 1) an intuitive interface for validated data entry; 2) audit trails for tracking data manipulation and export; 3) automated export procedures to common statistical packages; and 4) procedures for importing data from external sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State REDCap hosting, validation features, audit trail capability, export/import procedures, and how REDCap will be used in the study data workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleconferencing security, monitoring and logging
rubrics_metrics.description: International conference calls utilize either standard international long distance or a third-party teleconferencing service; both options require a secure pin. Calls to African countries are often actively monitored in house to ensure call stability; the monitor can respond immediately to poor connections and dropped callers via an electronic activity panel. A log of all calls is maintained and regularly reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document teleconference access controls (secure PINs), active monitoring for call quality, and maintenance/review of call logs for operational oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Videoconferencing infrastructure and secured hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: Videoconferences utilize Skype, Polycom or Adobe Connect. One conference room is equipped with advanced videoconferencing equipment (HD video cameras and projectors); all rooms have webcams and LCD screens; a keypad-secured dedicated control room houses the Adobe Connect server which is operable via an advanced remote control pad. Systems are supported in house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe available videoconf hardware, secured server hosting (keypad-secured control room), and in-house support to demonstrate reliable audiovisual collaboration capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign justification content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foreign Justification explains why the proposed K01 will be conducted in Uganda: the proposal develops geospatial and mathematical transmission models to identify regions where preventive therapy (PT) for TB provides most benefit. It states research is highly relevant to populations worldwide but would be difficult to conduct in US populations because the US has much lower HIV/TB co-infection prevalence and greater resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a project includes foreign research, justify the foreign site by explaining local disease burden, resource constraints, feasibility differences vs. the US, and how the work maximizes public health impact in the host country and beyond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH biosketch formatting exactly and respect the five-page maximum per person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Biographical Sketch sections and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Required components include: NAME; eRA Commons user name; POSITION TITLE; EDUCATION/TRAINING (begin with baccalaureate, include postdoctoral/residency, add/delete rows as necessary). The biosketch includes labeled sections A. Personal Statement, B. Positions and Honors, C. Contributions to Science (with peer-reviewed publications and manuscripts under review), and D. Research Support (ongoing and completed, role and dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit Personal Statement about research focus and mentorship, list positions and other experience, detail selected contributions to science with citations, and list current/previous research support with roles and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile form-field requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile fields include Prefix, First/Middle/Last Name, Position/Title, Organization Name, Department, Address, Country, Phone Number, E-Mail, Project Role (e.g., PD/PI), Degree Type, Other Project Role Category (e.g., Mentor, Co-Mentor), Degree Year, Attach Biographical Sketch (file name), Attach Current & Pending Support (file name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete profile metadata fields and attach required documents (biosketch, current & pending support) for each Senior/Key person as specified on the form.
